workItems.title: Prove Windows launcher architecture and packaging
workItems.objective: Prove a self-contained .NET 8 WPF x64 launcher, test project, LCARS shell, and unpackaged per-user deployment on Windows CI.
acceptance: Launcher and unit tests build on the repository Windows CI image.
The app runs without a machine-wide .NET runtime.
A minimal LCARS shell renders correctly at 100%, 150%, and 200% scale.
Packaging and replace-on-exit self-update options are documented with a recommendation.
No existing C++ target or release artifact regresses.

workItems.title: Implement deterministic STFC discovery and health model
workItems.objective: Discover bounded installation candidates, validate prime.exe targets, persist a user-confirmed selection, and expose a read-only health state.
acceptance: Discovery returns evidence and confidence for every candidate.
Wrong official-launcher directories are rejected.
Manual folder selection is supported.
A user-confirmed selection is persisted and revalidated.
Process, selection, and discovery health remain composable.
Non-ASCII and non-default paths are covered by tests.
No recursive drive scan occurs.

workItems.title: Publish a machine-readable Windows release manifest
workItems.objective: Generate and publish versioned release metadata with Windows artifact size and SHA-256.
acceptance: Manifest is generated from built artifacts, not handwritten.
Schema and release-channel semantics are documented.
CI validates manifest filename, size, and checksum against packaged files.
Existing direct version.dll and archive assets remain available.
validation: release workflow dry-run or fixture test

workItems.title: Implement transactional mod install, update, repair, and rollback
workItems.objective: Safely deploy verified version.dll artifacts with a persisted transaction journal and deterministic recovery.
acceptance: HTTP status, size, and SHA-256 are verified before staging.
Mutation is denied while STFC is running.
Existing manual installations can be adopted or backed up.
Interrupted commits recover or roll back deterministically.
Uninstall removes only managed artifacts and preserves config and logs.
validation: dotnet test including fault injection at every transaction boundary

workItems.title: Generate a shared mod configuration schema
workItems.objective: Create a versioned machine-readable schema from the mod’s authoritative defaults and metadata without introducing a second hand-maintained configuration truth.
acceptance: Schema includes types, defaults, platform support, descriptions, and restart behavior.
Release validation detects drift between C++ config loading and the schema.
Deprecated aliases are represented explicitly.
The existing TOML parser remains authoritative.

workItems.title: Build the schema-driven configuration editor
workItems.objective: Provide searchable, validated sparse TOML editing while preserving comments and unknown keys.
acceptance: Settings are generated from the shared schema.
A generated presentation envelope supplies player-facing labels, optional help, units, apply timing, grouping, search terms, and accessibility text without redefining runtime defaults or persistence.
The compact launcher home remains separate from the larger searchable settings workspace.
Normal settings render as a borderless full-row list with a stable control column; hover, selection, and keyboard focus remain distinct and additive.
Raw keys, value types, literal defaults, and runtime apply tokens remain searchable and available through explicit technical detail rather than the primary reading path.
Microsoft Fluent System Icons are exposed through an application-owned semantic icon layer with accessible names and consistent target sizes.
The title-area theme selector shows and marks the selected System, Light, or Dark color mode while leaving future visual styles as a separate extensibility point.
Reset is contextual to an existing override, while settings with meaningful inheritance preserve an explicit Default/On/Off distinction.
Notifications are grouped, searchable, and expandable without flattening meaningful event names or rendering every delivery control at once.
Hotkey alternatives render as individually removable chips with one Add action and no detached ambiguous unbind control.
The conditional dirty-state bar derives a visible apply-timing summary from all staged settings and reports mixed timing without hiding it in a tooltip.
Unknown keys and comments survive normal edits.
Save uses backup, validation, and atomic replacement.
Raw-file open and remove-override actions are available.
Invalid or unsupported TOML is never destructively rewritten.
validation: dotnet test with golden TOML fixtures

workItems.title: Implement launch and official game-update handoff
workItems.objective: Launch through the supported Windows path, track process state, delegate base-game updates to the official launcher, and re-check mod health afterward.
acceptance: Modded and explicit unmodded launch states are distinguishable.
Concurrent launch and mutation are prevented.
Official-launcher exit triggers game and mod health re-evaluation.
Offline launch remains available for an already healthy installation.
Failures are actionable and never silently reset the UI.
validation: dotnet test with fake process service

workItems.title: Add privacy-preserving diagnostics and repair UX
workItems.objective: Explain unhealthy states, offer bounded repairs, and export previewable redacted diagnostics without automatic upload.
acceptance: Every health failure maps to an explanation and safe next action.
Normal launcher UI omits filesystem paths, discovery provenance, and internal health detail unless the user explicitly opens diagnostics.
Diagnostic contents are previewed.
Fixture tests prove token, private path, and private endpoint redaction.
Repair never modifies files outside the allowlist.
No diagnostic data is uploaded automatically.

workItems.title: Implement launcher self-update
workItems.objective: Update the unpackaged launcher through a verified replace-on-exit helper with rollback.
acceptance: The running executable is never overwritten in place.
Update payload is verified by manifest size and SHA-256.
Failed startup restores the previous launcher.
Stable and prerelease channels remain explicit.
Offline use is unaffected.
validation: packaged upgrade and rollback smoke test

workItems.title: Integrate Windows launcher packaging, accessibility, and release gates
workItems.objective: Publish a production-ready Windows launcher without removing the manual version.dll distribution path.
acceptance: Windows CI builds, tests, and packages launcher and mod artifacts.
The executable, window, taskbar, shortcuts, and release surfaces use the approved multi-resolution STFC Mod Bridge application icon.
Keyboard, screen reader, reduced motion, and high-DPI smoke tests pass.
Clean install, adoption, update, game-update repair, rollback, uninstall, and offline launch are documented and smoked.
Manual version.dll assets and installation documentation remain supported.
Release checklist includes launcher-specific rollback and withdrawal steps.
